open: Predict transverse-mode instability in a Yb-doped fiber laser from its complete pumping history. Connect inversion-dependent defect production and bleaching to spatial heat deposition and mode coupling, including changes caused by reversing the order in which pump channels are raised.
status: Cui et al.’s 2026 experiments on a 4 kW integrated oscillator/amplifier changed instability onset from about 6.3 to 67 minutes through pumping sequence. Prioritizing the 915 nm forward pump reduced peak inversion; this supplies a sharp benchmark for a transferable model beyond one laser’s empirical optimization.
why: Reliable operating envelopes require accounting for evolving absorbing defects that couple optical aging to beam quality.
key_works: N. Cui, X. Yang, B. Gao, and L. Liu (2026), “Impact of the pumping sequences on the photodarkening-induced transverse mode instability in a 4 kW oscillating and amplifying integrated fiber laser,” [DOI:10.1016/j.yofte.2026.104653](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.yofte.2026.104653).

title: Suppressing BaF₂’s slow scintillation without sacrificing prompt photons
open: Develop bulk BaF₂ compositions suppressing self-trapped-exciton afterglow while preserving core-valence prompt light. A proposed census target is at least 100-fold suppression of slow photon yield with at least 90% retention of the undoped fast yield under matched excitation and collection calibration.
status: Xu et al.’s 2025 heavily Y-doped crystals reduced slow photon yield to roughly 6–10% of undoped values while retaining roughly 74–87% of fast yield, depending on boule position. These calibrated photon-yield ratios differ from radioluminescence spectral-intensity ratios; the proposed 100-fold/90% combination is not a reported record.
why: More prompt photons with less afterglow would reduce pileup and improve timing.
key_works: J. Xu et al. (2025), “Influence of Yttrium Concentration on Scintillation Performance of Heavily Y-Doped Barium Fluoride Crystals,” [DOI:10.1109/TNS.2025.3535633](https://doi.org/10.1109/TNS.2025.3535633).

title: Absolute branching into 150 ps core-to-core luminescence
open: Predict and measure the absolute fraction of deposited ionizing energy converted into the approximately 150 ps Ba-to-La core-to-core emission in BaF₂–LaF₃. Follow core-hole creation and competing relaxation channels across excitation energy and La concentration.
status: Shendrik et al. identified this component in 2025 above an excitation threshold near 24 eV and assigned it to recombination between Ba 5p electrons and La 5p holes. Identifying the transition and decay constant does not establish the usable energy-to-prompt-photon conversion efficiency.
why: A short lifetime improves timing substantially only when the excitation cascade supplies enough photons to that channel.
key_works: R. Shendrik et al. (2025), “Ultrafast core-to-core luminescence in BaF₂–LaF₃ single crystals,” [DOI:10.1038/s41598-025-11505-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-11505-w).

title: Ten-picosecond coincidence timing from clinically useful scintillator volumes
open: Produce a scintillator or metascintillator supporting 10 ps FWHM coincidence timing for 511 keV photon pairs while retaining useful stopping efficiency and energy discrimination in realistic thicknesses. Report event-selection efficiency so performance is not defined only by an unusually favorable subset.
status: The 10 ps objective remains explicit in Lecoq’s 2025 FAST workshop contribution. Orfano et al.’s 2024 nanocomposite/BGO multilayers demonstrate energy sharing and a 25% timing improvement relative to their monolithic BGO reference, leaving a substantial gap to the complete specification.
why: Ten-picosecond time-of-flight localization would change PET reconstruction, sensitivity, and dose tradeoffs.
key_works: M. Orfano et al. (2024), “Fast Emitting Nanocomposites for High-Resolution ToF-PET Imaging Based on Multicomponent Scintillators,” [DOI:10.1002/admt.202302075](https://doi.org/10.1002/admt.202302075); P. Lecoq (2025), “Harnessing the Purcell Effect for Faster Metascintillators,” [FAST2025 contribution](https://indico.cern.ch/event/1445926/contributions/6487549/).

title: Separating disorder and traps in garnet-scintillator nonproportionality
open: Predict how converting a fixed multication garnet composition from single crystal to ceramic changes gamma-ray light-yield nonproportionality. Independently constrain compositional disorder, carrier thermalization, and traps, then reproduce response versus energy without fitting all effects into one quenching constant.
status: Korzhik et al.’s 2025-online/2026-volume comparison measures Ce- and paired-activator materials across the (Gd,Y,Lu)₃(Al,Ga)₅O₁₂ family. The remaining inference problem is to identify which microscopic changes cause observed response differences and predict an unmeasured composition or processing route.
why: It would permit transparent ceramics to be designed for energy resolution alongside light output and speed.
key_works: M. Korzhik et al. (2026; online 2025), “Comparison of the response non-proportionality to gamma-rays in single crystalline and ceramic scintillation materials of the (Gd,Y,Lu)₃(Al,Ga)₅O₁₂ family,” [DOI:10.1016/j.nima.2025.171107](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nima.2025.171107).

title: The iron threshold for Zn-rich secondary-phase nucleation in CdZnTe
open: Establish the concentration and growth-condition thresholds at which trace iron nucleates Zn-rich secondary phases during traveling-heater growth of CdZnTe. Predict their location and density, then validate through controlled iron additions or removal.
status: Ünal et al. (2026) report three-dimensional ToF-SIMS evidence that iron co-localizes with Zn-rich phases in the last-to-solidify crystal region. This identifies a candidate nucleation pathway but does not establish its quantitative rate law or maximum tolerable iron concentration across thermal histories.
why: A chemically specific contamination limit could improve detector-grade boule yield and prevent localized charge-collection defects.
key_works: M. Ünal, S. S. Sedani, İ. Yıldız, Ö. B. Balbaşı, and R. Turan (2026), “Iron impurities drive Zn-rich phase formation in CdZnTe crystals,” [DOI:10.1016/j.matlet.2025.139521](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matlet.2025.139521).

title: Five-meV photocathodes at sustained milliampere current
open: Achieve mean transverse energy at or below 5 meV together with quantum efficiency of at least 5%, approximately 5 mA continuous current, and multiweek operation in a practical electron gun. This proposed census target seeks a tenfold MTE reduction while preserving the other operating metrics.
status: Wang et al.’s September 2026 preprint reports cryogenic K₂CsSb with 50 meV MTE, 5.4% quantum efficiency, operation at 5 mA, and an approximately 20-day operational history. This is a recent preprint benchmark; carrier survival, surface escape, disorder, and gun operation remain coupled constraints.
why: Lower intrinsic emittance at high average current would raise brightness for continuous-wave free-electron lasers and energy-recovery linacs.
key_works: D. Wang et al. (2026), “Ultralow Mean Transverse Energy and High Quantum Efficiency Cryogenic Bialkali Photocathode for MHz-Repetition-Rate Electron Sources,” [arXiv:2609.18137](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18137), preprint.

title: Is the clock-active thorium site a dimer or an isolated compensated substitution?
open: Discriminate competing assignments of the dominant quadrupole-split ²²⁹Th site in CaF₂: a thorium dimer or an isolated Th⁴⁺ substitution compensated by two fluorine interstitials. Obtain structural evidence specific to the optically interrogated clock population.
status: Rehn et al.’s July 2026 preprint argues that thermodynamics, DFT, and electric-field gradients favor an isolated substitution with an approximately 90° interstitial motif, challenging a dimer assignment. Agreement with a quadrupole spectrum alone need not uniquely establish atomic structure.
why: The distinction determines whether linewidth control requires preventing thorium aggregation or controlling fluoride compensation.
key_works: D. A. Rehn et al. (2026), “Defect assignment of the clock site in ²²⁹Th:CaF₂,” [arXiv:2607.12202](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12202); M. Guan et al. (2026), “Defect Dynamics and Isomer Quenching in ²²⁹Th:CaF₂ Crystals,” [arXiv:2609.38843](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38843), both preprints.

title: Engineering switchable nuclear-isomer quenching through host traps
open: Engineer host defects permitting rapid optical resetting of the ²²⁹Th isomer when activated while preserving a long radiative lifetime during interrogation. Establish a causal map from particular traps and charge states to site-specific quenching rates and controllable release pathways.
status: Terhune et al. measured photoinduced quenching in 2025 and proposed defect-assisted internal conversion. Guan et al.’s September 2026 preprint resolves eleven thermoluminescence peaks and links traps to temperature-dependent quenching; traps can also protect emission by sequestering carriers.
why: Controlled resetting could shorten clock cycles and improve readout without sacrificing protection during measurement.
key_works: J. E. S. Terhune et al. (2025), “Photoinduced quenching of the ²²⁹Th isomer in a solid-state host,” [DOI:10.1103/glzr-thyw](https://doi.org/10.1103/glzr-thyw); M. Guan et al. (2026), “Defect Dynamics and Isomer Quenching in ²²⁹Th:CaF₂ Crystals,” [arXiv:2609.38843](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38843).

title: A spinless nuclear-clock host without hidden VUV absorption
open: Synthesize a ²²⁹Th host whose surrounding nuclei introduce negligible magnetic-spin noise, whose thorium sites are sufficiently uniform, and which is transparent at the approximately 148 nm nuclear transition. Include excitonic and charge-transfer absorption in screening rather than relying on the electronic bandgap.
status: Morgan et al.’s September 2026 revision reports a decisive negative result: synthesized Th(SO₄)₂ is opaque at 148 nm because of charge-transfer excitons. This supersedes the optimistic 2025 proposal; apparently suitable bandgap and spin composition do not establish a working host.
why: Removing host nuclear-spin noise while preserving optical access could narrow solid-state nuclear-clock transitions.
key_works: H. W. T. Morgan et al. (2026 revision; first submitted 2025), “Investigation into thorium sulfate as a spinless crystal for a high-performance solid-state ²²⁹Th nuclear clock,” [arXiv:2503.11374v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.11374v2).

title: The material source of the cryogenic-detector low-energy excess
open: Identify the material process creating unexplained sub-keV phonon events in cryogenic calorimeters. Predict the event spectrum and relaxation from measured stresses, interfaces, and thermal history, distinguishing absorber stress release from sensor-only events without discarding genuine particle recoils.
status: A 2026 NUCLEUS study of a two-sensor sapphire detector found no evidence for radiation dependence in its tests, reduced initial rates with slower cooling, and decay approximately proportional to elapsed time⁻⁰·⁵⁹ ± ⁰·⁰⁶. These constraints have not identified a unique microscopic source.
why: This background limits low-mass dark-matter and coherent-neutrino-scattering searches as energy thresholds fall.
key_works: H. Abele et al., NUCLEUS Collaboration (2026), “Characterization of the low energy excess using a NUCLEUS Al₂O₃ detector,” [DOI:10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15950-3](https://doi.org/10.1140/epjc/s10052-026-15950-3).

title: Distinguishing bulk-flexoelectric boundary layers from surface piezoelectricity
open: Design a measurement separating genuine surface piezoelectricity from surface-localized response generated by bulk flexoelectricity. Independently vary sample size, surface termination, and electrical boundary conditions while resolving strain or field profiles.
status: Mohammadi et al.’s 2025 closed-form solutions show that finite flexoelectric bodies can respond near surfaces even under homogeneous loading. Such boundary layers resemble surface piezoelectric effects, creating an experimental attribution problem; the continuum boundary-layer calculation itself is already solved.
why: Reliable attribution is needed before large nanoscale coupling coefficients can be transferred to devices or used to infer symmetry.
key_works: H. Mohammadi, F. Greco, D. Codony, and I. Arias (2025), “Flexoelectricity causes surface piezoelectric-like effects in dielectrics,” [DOI:10.1016/j.ijmecsci.2025.110162](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijmecsci.2025.110162), [arXiv:2501.17626](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17626).

title: Three-dimensional trap geography in SrAl₂O₄:Eu,Dy afterglow
open: Determine the spatial distribution and connectivity of Eu emitters, Dy electron traps, and competing defects, then predict charging, afterglow, and thermoluminescence from that measured structure. Avoid separately refitting arbitrary trap-energy distributions or hopping networks to each experiment.
status: Optical work published in 2025 directly supports trapping at lanthanide codopants, including Dy. Koizumi et al.’s 2025 random-walk model reproduces several luminescence processes using an inferred one-dimensional trap landscape; connecting these effective models to independently measured three-dimensional geometry remains open.
why: It would make brightness, charging speed, and persistence jointly designable.
key_works: D. Van der Heggen, J. J. Joos, and P. F. Smet (2025), “Optical Evidence of Charge Trapping at Lanthanide Codopants in SrAl₂O₄:Eu,Ln (Ln = Nd, Sm, Dy) Persistent Phosphors,” [DOI:10.1002/adom.202402153](https://doi.org/10.1002/adom.202402153); R. Koizumi et al. (2025), “Visualization of trap distribution in SrAl₂O₄:Eu²⁺,Dy³⁺ … based on a random walk model,” [DOI:10.1039/D5CP01232E](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5CP01232E).

title: Spontaneous topological arrest in unpinned passive ring melts
open: Determine whether nonconcatenated passive ring melts undergo topological arrest above their ordinary segmental glass transition when no rings are externally immobilized. Establish chain-length and stiffness dependence while distinguishing broken ergodicity from a very long terminal relaxation time.
status: A topological-glass scenario was advanced in 2016. Molecular dynamics published in 2026 finds aging after thermal quenches and links persistent threading to relaxation; these simulations do not establish an experimentally observed unpinned transition.
why: It would establish whether topology supplies a distinct route to solidification and permit rheology programmed through chain architecture.
key_works: D. Michieletto and M. S. Turner (2016), “A topologically driven glass in ring polymers,” [paper](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4868430/); A. Behera et al. (2026), “Aging of ring polymeric topological glass formers via thermal quench,” [DOI:10.1103/tdfs-l7fw](https://doi.org/10.1103/tdfs-l7fw).

title: Linear-contamination threshold in ring-melt viscosity
open: Determine the linear-chain concentration creating a rubbery plateau or dominating zero-shear viscosity as a function of both ring and contaminant molecular weights. Recover intrinsic ring-melt viscosity with quantified uncertainty below the relevant contamination threshold.
status: The 2024 reassessment of moderately entangled ring melts identifies remaining purity and analytical-detection limits as obstacles to accurate viscosity measurements. Trace linear chains can obscure the terminal response precisely where competing descriptions of ring relaxation need stringent tests.
why: A calibrated threshold would make ring-rheology measurements comparable and prevent impurity-controlled relaxation from being mistaken for intrinsic topology.
key_works: K. Peponaki, D. Tsalikis, N. Patelis, G. Sakellariou, T. Chang, and D. Vlassopoulos (2024), “Revisiting the Viscosity of Moderately Entangled Ring Polymer Melts,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.macromol.4c00601](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.macromol.4c00601).

title: Experimental realization of colloidal-ring topological bigels
open: Realize the predicted bicomponent gel of polymers threaded through colloidal rings and measure its ring-radius threshold, connectivity, and terminal rheology. Show that network lifetime follows threading constraints rather than uncontrolled attractive aggregation.
status: Bonato, Marenduzzo, and Orlandini’s 2025 simulations predict a fluid-to-gel-like transition above a critical ring radius, with an analytical threshold estimate and slowed entanglement mobility. Experimental realization and finite-lifetime limits remain the next tests.
why: Such gels could obtain connectivity from removable geometric constraints without permanent cross-links.
key_works: A. Bonato, D. Marenduzzo, and E. Orlandini (2025), “Formation of Topological Bigels in Mixtures of Colloidal Rings and Polymers,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.188203](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.188203).

title: Predicting knot-specific mechanochemical scission
open: Predict how knot type, tightness, and backbone chemistry jointly determine polymer-chain scission location and force-dependent rate. Compare knot topologies and unknotted controls with matched chemical linkages and loading histories.
status: Zhang et al. demonstrated mechanical weakening by a molecular knot in 2024. That resolves the basic existence question for their architecture but does not provide a transferable law distinguishing geometric stress concentration, knot friction, and intrinsic bond reactivity.
why: Molecular knots could become predictable mechanophores rather than uncontrolled weak points.
key_works: M. Zhang, R. Nixon, F. Schaufelberger, L. Pirvu, G. De Bo, and D. A. Leigh (2024), “Mechanical scission of a knotted polymer,” [DOI:10.1038/s41557-024-01510-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-024-01510-3).

title: Autophobic dewetting versus core–ligand chemical mismatch
open: Separate matrix-chain entropy, particle curvature, and core–ligand chemical mismatch as causes of demixing in polymer-grafted nanoparticles. Predict whether increasing the matrix-to-graft chain-length ratio causes aggregation when these variables are independently controlled.
status: Koh et al.’s 2020 simulations of roughly 5 nm particles show no demixing at chain-length ratio ten without suitable attractions, whereas experiments on roughly 10–20 nm particles commonly demix above ratios around four. Introducing chemical-mismatch interactions reproduces behavior otherwise attributed to autophobicity.
why: Resolving the attribution would replace empirical compatibility rules with reliable nanocomposite design.
key_works: C. Koh, G. S. Grest, and S. K. Kumar (2020), “Assembly of Polymer-Grafted Nanoparticles in Polymer Matrices,” [DOI:10.1021/acsnano.0c05495](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.0c05495).

title: Entanglement threshold for nanotetrapod-promoted polymer flow
open: Determine the molecular-weight and entanglement-density crossover at which dispersed nanotetrapods lower polymer viscosity, including dependence on arm length and loading. Validate the crossover through independently measured chain dynamics across matched polymer series.
status: A 2025 study reports approximately an order-of-magnitude viscosity reduction in ultrahigh-molecular-weight polystyrene, while 9 kDa polystyrene shows no comparable enhancement. The authors identify chain-length dependence as future work and report an approximately tenfold absolute-viscosity discrepancy between dewetting analysis and rheometry.
why: A predictive crossover could make the additive useful across processing conditions while preserving long-chain mechanical performance.
key_works: J. Sarkar et al. (2025), “Nanotetrapods promote polymer flow through confinement induced packing frustration,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63555-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63555-3).

title: Elementary cellulose microfibril chain count and packing
open: Establish the number and cross-sectional arrangement of glucan chains in individual native, never-dried plant cellulose microfibrils, including genuine variation among tissues. Distinguish competing 18- and 24-chain structures using measurements constraining chain count independently of NMR peak assignments.
status: Cresswell et al.’s 2025 solid-state NMR study resolves six glucose environments and revises common crystallinity assignments. Its interior-to-surface ratio is consistent with an 18-chain arrangement but does not uniquely exclude alternatives, including 24-chain arrangements sharing that ratio.
why: The elementary cross-section determines accessible surface, enzyme binding, swelling, and cell-wall mechanics.
key_works: R. Cresswell et al. (2025), “Using Solid-State NMR to Understand the Structure of Plant Cellulose,” [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c14452](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c14452).

title: Temperature-dependent mechanisms of cellulose hornification
open: Determine which molecular changes cause irreversible loss of cellulose swelling during drying and why water retention and accessible surface change their relationship with drying temperature. Separate kinetic trapping, fibril coalescence, and chemical cross-linking.
status: Hornification has been recognized since the 1940s. A 2023 study frames it as kinetic trapping; 2025 pulp experiments find different water-retention–surface-accessibility correlations below and above 100 °C, supporting multiple mechanisms without uniquely identifying them.
why: Mechanistic control would preserve accessibility through drying for paper reuse, nanocellulose processing, and biomass conversion.
key_works: F. A. Sellman et al. (2023), “Hornification of cellulose-rich materials – A kinetically trapped state,” [DOI:10.1016/j.carbpol.2023.121132](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.carbpol.2023.121132); C. Moser and B. Sjöstrand (2025), “Hornification of Softwood and Hardwood Pulps Correlating with a Decrease in Accessible Surfaces,” [DOI:10.1021/acsomega.5c03470](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.5c03470).

title: Aqueous identity and lifetime of Posner-type calcium-phosphate clusters
open: Determine whether neutral Ca₉(PO₄)₆ clusters are persistent, appreciable solution species under relevant aqueous conditions. Measure their abundance and lifetime relative to protonated and compositionally variable aggregates, without inferring solution structures solely from dried solids.
status: The Posner-cluster hypothesis is longstanding. Revised calcium–phosphate association constants reported in 2024 substantially change speciation predictions; evidence for calcium-phosphate association alone does not uniquely establish the classic neutral cluster.
why: Correct solution species are essential to predictive models of bone mineralization, pathological calcification, and calcium-phosphate precipitation.
key_works: D. P. McDonogh, J. D. Gale, P. Raiteri, and D. Gebauer (2024), “Redefined ion association constants have consequences for calcium phosphate nucleation and biomineralization,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47721-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-47721-7).

title: Phase-resolved prestress during intrafibrillar collagen mineralization
open: Identify which transient calcium-phosphate phases generate each collagen expansion and contraction during mineral infiltration. Quantitatively connect water expulsion to prestress and determine how native bone stops mineral accumulation near its functional state.
status: Multimodal in situ experiments in 2025 combine Raman spectroscopy with small- and wide-angle X-ray scattering. They resolve early expansion, contraction, and later hydroxyapatite-associated expansion; the material resembles bone for approximately nine hours before overmineralizing, leaving phase-specific stress generation and self-limitation unresolved.
why: Matching mineral quantity alone cannot guarantee native toughness when hydration history and residual stress differ.
key_works: R. Kröger, E. Tong, L. Gower, A. J. Smith, and J. E. Parker (2025), “Dynamics of intrafibrillar collagen mineralization revealed by multimodal in situ analysis,” [DOI:10.1016/j.actbio.2025.10.047](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.actbio.2025.10.047).

title: Reproducing enamel crystallites’ defect sandwich
open: Manufacture apatite crystallites with controlled magnesium-rich layers flanking the sodium-, fluoride-, and carbonate-enriched core found in human enamel. Measure gradient-driven residual stress and preferential acid dissolution at matched morphology and overall composition.
status: The 2020 discovery establishes intr crystallite chemical heterogeneity and connects gradients to stress. Enamel-like crystal platforms reported in 2025 improve experimental access, but reproducing the complete gradient and isolating its mechanical–chemical effects remain distinct targets.
why: Gradient-controlled crystallites would clarify nanoscale caries susceptibility and guide restorative minerals.
key_works: K. A. DeRocher et al. (2020), “Chemical gradients in human enamel crystallites,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-2433-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2433-3); J. Chang et al. (2025), “Biomimetic Enamel-like Crystals: A Versatile Platform for Unraveling the Basic Mechanisms of Demineralization and Remineralization,” [DOI:10.1021/acsami.5c13544](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsami.5c13544).

title: Marine–freshwater discrepancy in nacre temperature sensitivity
open: Explain why nacre tablet thickness tracks temperature in studied marine mollusks while comparable freshwater studies find weak or absent relationships. Separate temperature from metabolism, carbonate chemistry, food supply, and control of the mineralization compartment.
status: Carskaddan et al.’s 2025 analysis finds temperature-associated differences across marine locations and time while contrasting freshwater null results from 2021 and 2023. The authors explicitly identify the reason for this difference as unknown.
why: It would reveal biological control of nacre assembly and determine when shell microstructure is a valid environmental proxy.
key_works: J. S. Carskaddan, M. C. Rillo, P. G. Harnik, and R. A. Metzler (2025), “Nacre microstructure records spatiotemporal variation in temperature in the modern ocean,” [DOI:10.3389/fmars.2025.1517327](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmars.2025.1517327).

title: Experimental antifreeze-protein engulfment-spacing exponent
open: Measure how the supercooling required to engulf an ice-bound antifreeze protein scales with independently measured separation between adsorbed proteins. Test inverse-square scaling while separating adsorption kinetics, protein dimensions, and ice-face orientation.
status: Thosar et al.’s 2024 simulations and interface theory predict an engulfment threshold proportional to inverse spacing squared, rather than the commonly assumed inverse-spacing law. Experimental validation requires protein positions and engulfment events resolved on the same interface.
why: The exponent determines which molecular dimensions and surface coverages govern freezing inhibition.
key_works: A. U. Thosar et al. (2024), “On the engulfment of antifreeze proteins by ice,” [DOI:10.1073/pnas.2320205121](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2320205121), [arXiv:2401.01271](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01271).

title: Experimental separation of AFGP desolvation barriers and binding strength
open: Independently measure adsorption barriers and bound-state stability of antifreeze glycoproteins as glycan density changes. Determine when extra glycosylation improves binding but slows the development of protective surface coverage.
status: Yang and Sun’s 2025 simulations predict that glycan-rich molecules incur a larger desolvation penalty despite favorable bound configurations, explaining a nonmonotonic activity trend. Direct kinetic measurements and prospective sequence tests remain necessary to establish the mechanism experimentally.
why: Binding affinity alone may be an inadequate design objective when adsorption must compete with ice growth.
key_works: W. Yang and Z. Sun (2025), “Adsorption Barrier Limits the Ice Inhibition Activity of Glycan-Rich Antifreeze Glycoproteins,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.langmuir.5c05077](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.langmuir.5c05077), [arXiv:2509.08360](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08360).

title: Causal sequence rules for spider-silk supercontraction
open: Identify causal molecular rules linking MaSp1 polyalanine length and MaSp2 repeat architecture to humidity-triggered contraction strain and force. Use matched sequence substitutions at controlled protein mixture, crystallinity, and spinning history.
status: Fazio et al.’s 2025 physically informed machine-learning study links sequence descriptors to supercontraction and develops an analytical model. Natural silks vary simultaneously in sequence, mixture, and processing; matched recombinant constructs remain needed to identify transferable causal rules.
why: Molecular control would permit predictable humidity-driven actuators and prevent unexpected dimensional changes in silk devices.
key_works: V. Fazio, A. D. Malay, K. Numata, N. M. Pugno, and G. Puglisi (2025), “A Physically-Based Machine Learning Approach Inspires an Analytical Model for Spider Silk Supercontraction,” [DOI:10.1002/adfm.202420095](https://doi.org/10.1002/adfm.202420095).

title: Structure-specific proton pathways in amyloid fibrils
open: Determine which hydrated structural motifs carry protons through amyloid assemblies and predict conductivity from sequence at fixed morphology, water activity, and orientation. Distinguish internal hydrogen-bond networks from surface-associated water using structural, isotope, and electrical measurements.
status: Navarro et al. (2024) demonstrate proton-conducting assemblies from three prion-inspired heptapeptides, with apparent activation energies spanning approximately 8–31 kJ mol⁻¹. These benchmarks do not uniquely identify conducting pathways or establish a transferable sequence-to-conductivity law.
why: A microscopic rule would make protein proton conductors predictable components of sensors and bioelectronic interfaces.
key_works: S. Navarro, A. Andrio, M. Díaz-Caballero, S. Ventura, and V. Compañ (2024), “Harnessing prion-inspired amyloid self-assembly for sustainable and biocompatible proton conductivity,” [DOI:10.1039/D4NA00303A](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4NA00303A).

title: Ligand accessibility through the intact soft protein corona
open: Predict the fraction and lifetime of accessible targeting ligands on nanoparticles in plasma while retaining the exchanging soft corona. Connect corona composition and conformation to binding activity without measurements that remove weakly associated proteins.
status: Joung et al.’s 2025 two-color fluorescence tracking measures antibody sensing in the presence of whole coronas formed from four model proteins and their mixtures. This establishes an in situ assay foothold; prediction in complex plasma with competitive exchange remains open.
why: Nominal ligand density can misrepresent the binding sites actually available during circulation.
key_works: H. Joung et al. (2025), “Evaluating the In Situ Effects of Whole Protein Coronas on the Biosensing of Antibody-Immobilized Nanoparticles Using Two-Color Fluorescence Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis,” [DOI:10.3390/nano15030220](https://doi.org/10.3390/nano15030220).

title: Physiological validation of stalk–pore lipid-nanoparticle escape
open: Determine whether the simulated stalk-to-pore pathway releases long RNA under measured endosomal pH, hydration, and membrane-tension trajectories. Quantify its rate and contribution relative to alternative routes without choosing imposed conditions specifically to trigger escape.
status: Singh et al.’s 2026 study follows four approximately 20–30 μs simulations using MC3-containing particles and 12-base-pair DNA cargo. Imposed deprotonation and tension promote pore formation and release; these trajectories do not establish physiological rates or therapeutic-length mRNA escape.
why: Identifying the relevant membrane event would connect ionizable-lipid chemistry to the actual delivery bottleneck.
key_works: A. P. Singh, K. Shibata, Y. Miyazaki, and W. Shinoda (2026), “pH-Sensitive Amino Lipid-Driven Pore Formation Enables Endosomal Escape of Lipid Nanoparticles,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-76810-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-76810-y).

title: Predicting lipoprotein-driven internal nanoparticle remodeling
open: Predict how plasma lipoprotein exchange changes lipid-nanoparticle composition, internal phase, and cargo retention over time. Establish whether relations measured in model liquid-crystalline particles transfer to RNA-loaded formulations and different plasma samples.
status: Caselli et al.’s September 2026 study demonstrates lipid transfer using fluorescence, scattering, and microscopy. Cubic particles remodel substantially, while inverse-hexagonal particles retain structure despite exchange; predictive transfer across compositions and cargo states remains open.
why: Biological behavior can depend on evolving internal structure as well as the adsorbed surface layer.
key_works: L. Caselli et al. (2026), “Lipoprotein Corona Reshapes the Internal Structure of Lipid Nanoparticles,” [DOI:10.1021/acsnano.6c09400](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.6c09400).

title: Transfer limits of SAXS potency descriptors after lyophilization
open: Determine which formulations, cell types, and administration routes preserve the relation between internal nanoparticle order and post-storage activity. Identify necessary additional descriptors while separating structural disorder from RNA damage and lipid chemistry.
status: Chen et al. (2026) examine 58 mRNA-nanoparticle samples altered by freezing and lyophilization. SAXS peak intensity correlates strongly with in vitro activity under the studied conditions, but the authors explicitly find the relationship context-dependent and unsuitable for direct in vivo extrapolation.
why: A calibrated descriptor could accelerate storage qualification without relying on an unreliable potency surrogate.
key_works: X. Chen et al. (2026), “Loss of internal structural order induced by freezing and lyophilization correlates with reduced in vitro activity of mRNA lipid nanoparticles,” [DOI:10.1016/j.jconrel.2026.115148](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jconrel.2026.115148).

title: A falsifiable test of spinorial hastatic order in URu₂Si₂
open: Identify and measure an observable distinguishing spinorial hybridization from competing multipolar explanations of URu₂Si₂ hidden order, including across the pressure-induced antiferromagnetic transition. Explain the symmetry breaking and elusive magnetic signatures with one parameter-consistent model.
status: The parent hidden-order problem dates to 1985. Kornjača and Flint’s 2023 theory unifies candidate hastatic and antiferromagnetic phases and identifies additional vector observables, but remains a discriminating proposal rather than experimental identification.
why: It would establish or exclude an unusual form of spinorial order and constrain correlated-electron hybridization theories.
key_works: M. Kornjača and R. Flint (2023), “Unified theory of hastatic order and antiferromagnetism in URu₂Si₂,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.108.085133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.108.085133).

title: Order parameters on both sides of UTe₂’s internal high-field boundary
open: Determine the superconducting representations, nodal structures, and relative component phases on either side of the internal boundary for field parallel to the b axis. Reproduce ultrasound mode selectivity, magnetostriction, and the local tetracritical diagram.
status: A 2026 study reports the bulk boundary near 14–15 T and a tetracritical point near 13.5 T and 1.25 K using ultrasound down to 0.33 K and up to 18 T. The September revision constrains multicomponent superconductivity without uniquely assigning both states.
why: It would connect field-stabilized pairing theories to a thermodynamically established phase diagram.
key_works: M. Vališka et al. (2026), “Thermodynamic Evidence of Tetracritical Topology in the H–T Phase Diagram of UTe₂ for H ∥ b,” [arXiv:2604.25896v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25896v3), [DOI:10.1103/1l46-jbm6](https://doi.org/10.1103/1l46-jbm6).

title: Species-resolved pair breaking by UTe₂ interstitial defects
open: Establish a causal relation between a measured defect species and UTe₂’s transition temperature, residual quasiparticle density, and split transitions. Controlled defect introduction or removal must separate interstitial effects from uranium vacancies, strain, and compositional gradients.
status: Sample dependence has persisted since superconductivity was reported in 2019. Kengle et al. (2025) find interstitial defects in Te2 layers and no uranium vacancies in the examined samples; the resulting explanation needs quantitative, independently controlled validation.
why: It would turn sample quality into a defined physical variable and sharpen unconventional pair-breaking tests.
key_works: C. S. Kengle, N. Schnitzer, M. M. Bordelon, S. M. Thomas, and P. F. S. Rosa (2025), “What causes the variation in superconducting properties of UTe₂?”, [arXiv:2509.20298](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.20298).

title: YbB₁₂’s missing magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations
open: Explain why quantum oscillations occur in electrical transport and magnetocaloric measurements of insulating YbB₁₂ but remain absent in the measured elastic response of the same crystal. Predict amplitudes and upper bounds across probes, including the change after metallization.
status: Kurihara et al.’s 2026 study reaches 65 T and 485 mK, observes transport and magnetocaloric oscillations, and finds no corresponding insulating-phase magnetoacoustic oscillations; elastic oscillations appear in the metallic phase. This null result constrains neutral-fermion and charged-band mechanisms.
why: It tests proposed neutral Fermi surfaces and their coupling to strain.
key_works: R. Kurihara et al. (2026), “Search for magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations in the insulating phase of YbB₁₂,” [arXiv:2605.04350](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04350), [DOI:10.1103/m3gy-g9tv](https://doi.org/10.1103/m3gy-g9tv).

title: FFLO modulation versus triplet pair-density waves in CeCoIn₅’s Q phase
open: Measure condensate spatial modulation and spin structure directly enough to distinguish an FFLO-modulated d-wave state from one containing a triplet pair-density wave. Reproducing magnetic-domain switching alone does not discriminate theories.
status: The interpretation has been contested since at least the 2014 domain-switching experiment. Gerber et al. infer inhomogeneous triplet pairing; Hatakeyama and Ikeda (2015) reproduce the switching with FFLO modulation and no triplet component.
why: It would identify the pairing response to strong paramagnetic pair breaking in a bulk superconductor.
key_works: S. Gerber et al. (2014), “Switching of magnetic domains reveals spatially inhomogeneous superconductivity,” [DOI:10.1038/nphys2833](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys2833); Y. Hatakeyama and R. Ikeda (2015), “Antiferromagnetic order oriented by Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov superconducting order,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.91.094504](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.91.094504).

title: A phase-sensitive sign test for nodeless CeCu₂Si₂
open: Determine whether the fully opened superconducting gap reverses sign between relevant electronic states using a phase-sensitive junction or calibrated impurity-interference experiment. Discriminate sign-preserving s wave, sign-changing s wave, and matrix-pairing interpretations without assuming the impurity potential.
status: The modern nodeless-gap controversy has developed over the past decade. Zhao et al. (2022) predict a quasiparticle-interference test for s± pairing; the 2023 review documents why a full gap alone does not settle the order parameter.
why: It would resolve a central ambiguity in the first heavy-fermion superconductor.
key_works: S. Zhao et al. (2022), “Revealing sign-reversal s±-wave pairing by quasiparticle interference in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeCu₂Si₂,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevB.105.014501](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.105.014501); M. Smidman et al. (2023), “Colloquium: Unconventional fully gapped superconductivity in the heavy-fermion metal CeCu₂Si₂,” [DOI:10.1103/RevModPhys.95.031002](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.95.031002).

title: UBe₁₃’s [111]-selective 6–10 T thermodynamic anomaly
open: Identify whether the high-field anomaly observed only for fields along [111] represents a phase transition, multipolar instability, or Fermi-surface crossover. Account for directional selectivity and signatures in magnetization and specific heat.
status: Shimizu et al. report this specific frontier in December 2025: anomalies in the 6–10 T range coexist with recovery of Fermi-liquid behavior at high fields. Multipolar correlations and electronic reconstruction remain candidate interpretations.
why: It would expose degrees of freedom hidden within UBe₁₃’s non-Fermi-liquid normal state.
key_works: Y. Shimizu et al. (2025), “Field-induced anomaly in the anisotropic non-Fermi-liquid normal state of UBe₁₃,” [DOI:10.1103/bxq6-tznr](https://doi.org/10.1103/bxq6-tznr).

title: Conditions for reproducible magnetism in RuO₂
open: Determine which combinations of stoichiometry, defects, strain, and interfaces produce magnetic order in RuO₂, establishing associated spin splitting independently of transport inference. Reconcile bulk null results and magnetic-film reports on quantitatively characterized sample series.
status: The altermagnetism controversy remains active. Qian et al. (2026) find clean bulk crystals consistent with paramagnetism, while Rezaei et al. (2026) report complex strain- and substrate-dependent film behavior. Intrinsic bulk altermagnetism is not settled.
why: It determines whether the oxide realizes the magnetic symmetry required for proposed spintronic functions.
key_works: T. Qian et al. (2026), “Determining the nature of magnetism in altermagnetic candidate RuO₂,” [DOI:10.1103/s98c-nkgj](https://doi.org/10.1103/s98c-nkgj); N. Rezaei et al. (2026), “Complex magnetic behavior in RuO₂ thin films driven by strain and substrate effects,” [DOI:10.1038/s43246-026-01292-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43246-026-01292-w).

title: Loop-current order versus probe-dependent symmetry breaking in CsV₃Sb₅
open: Determine whether a bulk loop-current pattern exists, identify its symmetry and onset temperature, and predict which probes detect it. Reconcile positive time-reversal-breaking reports with null Kerr measurements while separating domain effects from artifacts.
status: The controversy predates 2023. Cha et al. (2026) report circular-dichroism photoemission evidence for time-reversal breaking above charge order; Saykin et al. (2023) find no corresponding Kerr signal in their high-resolution experiment. Neither alone fixes the microscopic current pattern.
why: It would identify the normal-state symmetry from which kagome superconductivity emerges.
key_works: J. Cha et al. (2026), “Evidence of time-reversal symmetry breaking above the charge density wave order in a kagome metal,” [DOI:10.1038/s41567-026-03331-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-026-03331-2); D. R. Saykin et al. (2023), “High Resolution Polar Kerr Effect Studies of CsV₃Sb₅: Tests for Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking below the Charge-Order Transition,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.016901](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.016901).

title: Bulk charge-6e coherence versus mesoscopic flux harmonics
open: Establish whether kagome superconductors support a thermodynamic charge-6e condensate. Use independent fractional-vortex, Josephson, and geometry-scaling measurements to discriminate higher-charge order from multicomponent charge-2e metastability.
status: Ge et al. (2024) report h/4e and h/6e oscillations in CsV₃Sb₅ rings. Zhang, Wang, and Hu’s theory supplies another route to h/6e periodicity through metastable winding states and chiral domain walls, making periodicity alone an ambiguous condensate identifier.
why: It would establish superconducting order beyond ordinary Cooper-pair condensation.
key_works: J. Ge et al. (2024), “Charge-4e and Charge-6e Flux Quantization and Higher Charge Superconductivity in Kagome Superconductor Ring Devices,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevX.14.021025](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.14.021025); L.-F. Zhang, Z. Wang, and X. Hu (2024), “Higgs-Leggett mechanism for the elusive φ₀/3 = hc/6e oscillation in Little-Parks setup of Kagome superconductor CsV₃Sb₅,” [DOI:10.1038/s42005-024-01663-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42005-024-01663-0).

title: Separating excitonic and lattice causes of the Ta₂NiSe₅ gap
open: Identify a controlled perturbation separating excitonic instability from the coupled structural distortion, and determine which mechanism is sufficient to open the gap. Explain gating, structural domain boundaries, and local spectra together.
status: Wei et al. (2025) find gate-dependent behavior favoring a lattice-driven transition, whereas Bae et al.’s December 2025 preprint interprets domain-boundary measurements as evidence for dominant excitonic instability. The 2026 correction to the gating paper changes an energy-axis unit, not this stated interpretation.
why: It would distinguish an electronic condensate from a structural semiconductor with strong electronic feedback.
key_works: K. Wei et al. (2025), “Gate tuning of coupled electronic and structural phase transition in atomically thin Ta₂NiSe₅,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-66594-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66594-y); S. Bae et al. (2025), “Microscopic evidence of dominant excitonic instability in Ta₂NiSe₅,” [arXiv:2512.03011](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03011).

title: Identifying the one-ninth plateau state in YCOB
open: Determine the order and excitation statistics of the one-ninth magnetization plateau in YCu₃(OH)₆Br₂[Brₓ(OH)₁₋ₓ]. Discriminate Dirac-spinon, chiral topological, and translation-breaking interpretations through thermodynamics, spectroscopy, and disorder dependence.
status: The plateau was reported in 2024. Zheng et al. (2025) measure heat capacity to 41.5 T and 0.46 K and find behavior consistent with fermionic excitations, but the evidence does not uniquely establish topological order.
why: This small plateau provides a precise material test of fractionalization in frustrated magnets.
key_works: S. Jeon et al. (2024), “One-ninth magnetization plateau stabilized by spin entanglement in a kagome antiferromagnet,” [DOI:10.1038/s41567-023-02318-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-023-02318-7); G. Zheng et al. (2025), “Thermodynamic Evidence of Fermionic Behavior in the Vicinity of One-Ninth Plateau in a Kagome Antiferromagnet,” [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevX.15.021076](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.15.021076).

title: The dmit-131 residual thermal-conductivity discrepancy
open: Resolve why nominally equivalent β′-EtMe₃Sb[Pd(dmit)₂]₂ crystals yield incompatible conclusions about mobile gapless excitations. A specimen-exchange experiment should quantify thermal contacts, cooling history, disorder, and low-temperature extrapolation on shared samples.
status: Large residual heat conduction reported in 2010 conflicts with two 2019 studies reporting no such term. Kato et al. (2022) test the cooling-rate explanation and find no corresponding changes in structure, resistivity, or NMR; a generally accepted reconciliation remains lacking.
why: The discrepancy determines whether a leading organic spin-liquid candidate carries mobile neutral quasiparticles.
key_works: R. Kato, M. Uebe, S. Fujiyama, and H. Cui (2022), “A Discrepancy in Thermal Conductivity Measurement Data of Quantum Spin Liquid β′-EtMe₃Sb[Pd(dmit)₂]₂,” [DOI:10.3390/cryst12010102](https://doi.org/10.3390/cryst12010102), [arXiv:2201.07073](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.07073).

title: The positive thermal Hall mechanism in GdZnPO
open: Identify the excitations producing positive transverse heat transport in honeycomb spiral-spin-liquid candidate GdZnPO. Distinguish transport or scattering by spin and momentum vortices from weak anisotropic-exchange effects, reproducing field and temperature dependence quantitatively.
status: Zhao et al. (2025) report magnetic heat conduction down to approximately 50 mK and positive thermal Hall response at higher temperatures. Idealized ordered-state spin-wave models give zero Chern numbers; vortices, weak perturbations, and quantum effects remain possible missing ingredients.
why: It would connect a measured transport coefficient to the topology of a spiral manifold in a real material.
key_works: Y. Zhao et al. (2025), “Itinerant and topological excitations in a honeycomb spiral spin liquid candidate,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63620-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63620-x), [arXiv:2508.18795](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18795).

title: Separating CISS spin filtering from magnetochiral charge trapping
open: Determine how much magnetoresistance in ferromagnet–chiral-material devices reflects transmitted-spin polarization and how much arises from trapping or electrostatic history. Measure spin independently while varying bias sign, magnetization, relaxation time, and contact geometry.
status: Zhao et al. (2025) propose magnetochiral charge pumping; Tirion and van Wees (2025) challenge its bias dependence and propose a bias-induced electrostatic mechanism. Large electrical asymmetry alone does not resolve the distinction.
why: It would establish reliable measurement standards and design rules for chiral spin-selective materials.
key_works: Y. Zhao et al. (2025), “Magnetochiral charge pumping due to charge trapping and skin effect in chirality-induced spin selectivity,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-55433-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-55433-1); S. H. Tirion and B. J. van Wees (2025), “Bias-induced electrostatic magnetoresistance in ferromagnet/chiral systems,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-65680-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-65680-5).

title: The FeSb₂–FeAs₂ phonon-drag thermopower contrast
open: Predict why FeAs₂ can have substantially higher lattice thermal conductivity yet much smaller peak thermopower than FeSb₂. Identify the carrier–phonon momentum-transfer and defect parameters controlling the contrast.
status: Du et al. (2021) link FeSb₂’s sample-sensitive colossal thermopower to vacancies and structural distortions but explicitly leave the FeAs₂ contrast unexplained: approximately an order-of-magnitude larger thermal conductivity accompanies roughly sixfold smaller peak thermopower in the compared data.
why: It would permit deliberate tuning of low-temperature phonon-drag thermoelectrics instead of reliance on exceptional crystals.
key_works: Q. Du et al. (2021), “Vacancy defect control of colossal thermopower in FeSb₂,” [DOI:10.1038/s41535-020-00308-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41535-020-00308-z).

title: Equilibrium order versus arrested proton disorder in ice XIX
open: Determine ice XIX’s equilibrium proton configuration and configurational entropy separately from kinetically arrested disorder. Use convergent annealing, isotope-controlled calorimetry, and diffraction to establish whether observed partial order approaches a unique equilibrium state.
status: Structural models already exist. Gasser et al. (2024) recover about 25 ± 3% of the Pauling entropy and show strong isotope-dependent kinetics, including small H₂O additions enabling ordering in D₂O samples that otherwise fail to transform under the tested anneals.
why: It would separate thermodynamic residual entropy from kinetic arrest in a defined hydrogen-bond network.
key_works: T. M. Gasser, A. V. Thoeny, A. D. Fortes, and T. Loerting (2024), “Configurational entropy of ice XIX and its isotope effect,” [DOI:10.1038/s41598-024-61250-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-61250-9).

title: Ten-year novel desalination materials under the XPRIZE target
open: Demonstrate a novel desalination material or method treating seawater to potable quality at competitive cost and sustainability, with a substantiated operational lifetime of at least ten years. Meet selectivity, throughput, chemical durability, and real-feed fouling requirements together.
status: XPRIZE Water Scarcity launched in 2024. Track B is in semifinals, with semifinal testing scheduled for Q4 2026 and final testing for Q3 2027; the ten-year operational lifetime is an explicit target requiring credible lifetime substantiation within the competition schedule.
why: It connects separation-media performance to the service life and total cost needed for dependable water infrastructure.
key_works: XPRIZE Foundation (2025–2026), “XPRIZE Water Scarcity—Track B: Desalination: Novel Materials and Methods,” [official competition and guidelines](https://www.xprize.org/competitions/water).
prize: Track B final awards: US$8 million first place, US$1 million second, and US$500,000 third; milestone awards are separate.

title: Microscopic trigger of light-erased clay hydration hysteresis
open: Determine which microscopic excitation allows near-infrared illumination to release metastable hydration states in swelling clay. Predict the action spectrum, absorbed-power threshold, isotope dependence, and layer-spacing transition while separating local heating from direct excitation of confined water.
status: Teng and colleagues eliminated hydration hysteresis in synthetic Laponite in 2025 using 785 nm illumination with bulk-temperature control. Their measurements support optically activated nucleation; the microscopic energy-transfer channel and wavelength-dependent rate law remain follow-up targets.
why: A mechanism would make optical control of mineral hydration predictable and test how confined water crosses metastable free-energy barriers.
key_works: Y. Teng, C. Chen, L. Zheng, and M. L. Whittaker (2025), “Optically Triggered Nucleation Eliminates Hydration Hysteresis in Swelling Minerals,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.langmuir.4c04468](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.langmuir.4c04468).

title: Equilibrium versus drying-induced interstratification at the clay swelling crossover
open: Establish whether the mixed nematic, crystalline, and interstratified states between osmotic and crystalline swelling represent equilibrium coexistence or structures selected by drying. Determine their reversibility, phase boundaries, and relaxation times under independently controlled water activity and counterion composition.
status: Hotton and colleagues followed the complete crossover in levitated beidellite droplets in 2025. Layer separations decreased continuously to approximately 30 Å before entering a mixed regime; determining equilibrium versus protocol-dependent selection is a further question arising from the continuously drying geometry.
why: It would establish when clay water-retention curves describe equilibrium and when they encode processing history.
key_works: C. Hotton, T. Bizien, C. Hamon, É. Ferrage, and E. Paineau (2025), “Bridging the Gap between Osmotic and Crystalline Swelling in 2D Layered Materials Using Levitated Droplets,” [DOI:10.1002/smll.202505038](https://doi.org/10.1002/smll.202505038).

title: Experimental proton conduction along montmorillonite edges
open: Measure proton transport specifically along hydrated montmorillonite edges, separating it from interlayer conduction and dissolved-electrolyte transport. Test the predicted dependence on pH, magnesium substitution, edge connectivity, and hydrogen–deuterium exchange.
status: Feng and colleagues’ 2026 simulations found direct and water-assisted proton transfer along clay edges, with connectivity and barriers controlled by local chemistry. Nanosecond molecular trajectories establish a candidate mechanism; whether these exchanges generate a measurable edge-specific conduction channel remains experimentally unresolved.
why: It would connect mineral acid–base chemistry to macroscopic electrical transport.
key_works: Y. Feng, X. R. Advincula, H. Fang, and C. Schran (2026), “Clay Edges Are Dynamic Proton-Conducting Networks Modulated by Structure and pH,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.5c03748](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.5c03748); [arXiv:2508.15401](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15401).

title: Dissolved-gas enhancement of compacted-clay swelling pressure
open: Test whether dissolved gases increase clay swelling pressure through preferential interlayer partitioning when water activity, external pressure, and counterion chemistry are fixed. Separate this contribution from bubbles, desaturation, and gas-induced chemical reactions.
status: Owusu and colleagues’ 2026 molecular simulations predict gas-dependent pressure increases reaching approximately 1.5 MPa under their modeled conditions. This is a calculated increment; its contribution to the response of a compacted specimen containing both interlayer and interparticle porosity still requires experimental isolation.
why: It would improve predictions for gas-generating waste barriers and underground gas-storage seals.
key_works: J. P. Owusu, K. Karalis, N. I. Prasianakis, A. Ferrari, and S. V. Churakov (2026), “Swelling of Na-montmorillonite in the presence of dissolved gas molecules,” [DOI:10.1016/j.clay.2025.108058](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clay.2025.108058).

title: The suction–swelling-pressure discrepancy in compacted smectite
open: Explain the systematic gap between microscopic suction predictions and measured macroscopic swelling pressure at comparable dry density. Determine whether larger-scale tactoid and pore hierarchies close it, or whether equilibration, boundary conditions, or constitutive assumptions supply another missing contribution.
status: Zheng and Bourg’s 2026 simulations contain approximately 1,400 clay particles at the 0.1 μm scale, yet predict swelling pressures about 0.9 logarithmic units above experiment. Their suggested convergence scale near 2 μm is an extrapolation, not a demonstrated representative volume.
why: It would connect molecular clay forces to engineering stresses without empirical rescaling.
key_works: X. Zheng and I. C. Bourg (2026), “Microstructure, Transport, and Mechanics of Compacted Clay Simulated at the 0.1 μm Scale …,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpcc.6c00004](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcc.6c00004).

title: Location and fate of tetrahedral iron during ferrihydrite aging
open: Locate tetrahedrally coordinated Fe(III) within ferrihydrite and identify the rearrangements that reduce its population during aging. Distinguish particle-interior motifs, hydrated surface sites, and defects, and establish whether dehydration causes the coordination change.
status: Sassi and colleagues compared fresh ferrihydrite with material aged for five years in a 2024 study. Spectroscopy linked aging and dehydration to a decreasing tetrahedral-to-octahedral iron ratio, but the measurements do not uniquely locate the sites or establish the atomic transformation pathway.
why: Site assignments would improve predictions of contaminant binding, iron exchange, and mineral transformation.
key_works: M. Sassi et al. (2024), “Influence of time and ageing conditions on the properties of ferrihydrite,” [DOI:10.1039/D3EN00828B](https://doi.org/10.1039/D3EN00828B).

title: Operando charge compensation and branch selection in vivianite oxidation
open: Resolve how electron loss, water deprotonation, hydrogen defects, and lattice rearrangement couple during hydrated vivianite oxidation. Explain which conditions select a metavivianite intermediate and which bypass it, using simultaneous iron-valence, proton-release, and structural measurements.
status: Sassi and Rosso’s 2025 calculations predict metavivianite stabilization over an intermediate range of approximately 66–33% residual Fe(II). Chiba and colleagues experimentally demonstrated oxidation paths bypassing metavivianite in 2020; the remaining question is conditional pathway selection and charge compensation.
why: It would clarify phosphorus retention and the stability of recovered iron-phosphate products.
key_works: M. Sassi and K. M. Rosso (2025), “Insights into the Oxidation Mechanism of Vivianite to Metavivianite from First-Principles Calculations,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c07790](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c07790); K. Chiba et al. (2020), “The synthesis of metavivianite and the oxidation sequence of vivianite,” [DOI:10.2465/jmps.200417](https://doi.org/10.2465/jmps.200417).

title: Atomic identity of clay-stabilized labile Fe(III)
open: Identify the coordination, nuclearity, and location of reactive Fe(III) retained when montmorillonite modifies Fe(II)-catalyzed ferrihydrite transformation. Measure exchange between interlayer species, external adsorption sites, and nascent iron-oxide structures.
status: Wei and colleagues showed in 2025 that clay–ferrihydrite interactions alter recrystallization and can suppress magnetite formation while retaining reactive iron. Selective extraction establishes an operationally defined labile fraction; assigning that fraction to specific molecular species is the narrower remaining target.
why: It would connect measured reactive-iron inventories to mechanisms of contaminant mobilization.
key_works: H. Wei et al. (2025), “Nano-Scale Insights into Clay Minerals Regulating the Fe(II)-Catalyzed Ferrihydrite Transformation under Anoxic Conditions,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.4c11232](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.4c11232).

title: Electron acceptor in emerald-green photooxidation
open: Identify the electron acceptor and reaction sequence that convert arsenic(III) to arsenic(V) in illuminated emerald-green pigment. Close electron and atom balances among oxygen, acetate ligands, possible transient Cu(I), arsenolite, and the final arsenic(V)-rich material.
status: Carboni Marri and colleagues established distinct light- and humidity-driven degradation pathways in 2025. Their paper explicitly leaves the oxidative reaction partner and intermediate sequence unresolved; predominantly Cu(II) final products cannot establish whether transient Cu(I) participates.
why: Identifying the partner would reveal which environmental or binder controls can suppress arsenic migration.
key_works: S. Carboni Marri et al. (2025), “Discovering the dual degradation pathway of emerald green in oil paints: The effects of light and humidity,” [DOI:10.1126/sciadv.ady1807](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.ady1807).

title: Intrinsic trigger of irreversible Prussian-blue framework cleavage
open: Identify what initiates irreversible destruction of the iron–cyanide network in historically prepared Prussian-blue paint. Separate the effects of precursor defects, synthesis residues, neighboring pigments, and binder oxidation on formation of iron oxyhydroxides and iron–organic products.
status: Monico and colleagues’ 2026 study identified goethite-like Fe(III) alteration products and Fe(II) compounds consistent with oxalates while controlling measurement-induced photoreduction. They explicitly report that the intrinsic factors initiating alteration still lack definitive answers.
why: It would distinguish recoverable redox fading from destruction of the chromophore’s coordination framework.
key_works: L. Monico et al. (2026), “Illuminating Prussian blue fading in oil paintings: a multi-scale and multi-technique approach to mitigate synchrotron radiation X-ray induced iron photoreduction,” [DOI:10.1007/s12210-026-01410-3](https://doi.org/10.1007/s12210-026-01410-3).

title: Noncrystalline copper species behind fresco blackening
open: Identify the poorly crystalline or amorphous copper species that darken alkaline fresco paint when crystalline CuO cannot explain the color. Determine their formation pathway and optical contribution separately from particle aggregation and pigment impurities.
status: Jiménez-Desmond and colleagues’ 2026 comparison of eight pigments found that crystalline oxides did not account for all blackening. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated an additional reduced-copper contribution, but a combined Cu(I)/Cu(0) signal does not uniquely identify its phase or optical mechanism.
why: It would improve diagnoses and prevent treatments based on an incomplete tenorite-only explanation.
key_works: D. Jiménez-Desmond et al. (2026), “Blackening of copper pigments in wall paintings: impact of the fresco technique and the chemical composition of the pigments,” [DOI:10.1038/s40494-026-02461-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s40494-026-02461-3).

title: Humidity thresholds and memory in layered bronze disease
open: Predict when chloride-bearing archaeological copper resumes autocatalytic corrosion after a humidity excursion, using its CuCl distribution, surviving metal contacts, and soluble-salt inventory. Determine whether arrest and restart thresholds depend on hydration history.
status: Thunberg, Emmerson, and Watkinson varied relative humidity from 15% to 80% at 20 °C in 2025 experiments. Copper contact and soluble chloride formation changed reaction behavior; extending these controlled results to stratified patinas under repeated humidity cycles remains an engineering and reaction–diffusion problem.
why: Object-specific restart criteria would support better storage and emergency-drying decisions.
key_works: J. Thunberg, N. Emmerson, and D. Watkinson (2025), “New Evidence of the Relationship Between Oxidative Hydrolysis of CuCl ‘Bronze Disease’ and Relative Humidity …,” [DOI:10.3390/heritage8090350](https://doi.org/10.3390/heritage8090350).

title: Dark dissolution versus photocorrosion in cadmium–zinc sulfide pigments
open: Quantify the fractions of Cd–Zn sulfide pigment loss caused by dark dissolution and light-driven oxidation inside aged paint. Close metal and sulfur balances while independently controlling composition, polymorph, particle size, water activity, and binder ligands.
status: Castagnotto and colleagues’ 2025 study found strong light-driven activity in nanosized cubic compositions containing 20% or 40% zinc, together with lower but measurable dark ion release. The unresolved extension is quantitative pathway partitioning within a binder-confined historical paint layer.
why: It would establish whether limiting light addresses the dominant degradation route.
key_works: E. Castagnotto, S. Alberti, M. Campolucci, P. Manfrinetti, M. Ferretti, and F. Locardi (2025), “Photocorrosion Stability of CdxZn1–xS Yellow-Orange Pigments,” [DOI:10.1021/acs.chemmater.4c03274](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemmater.4c03274).

title: Causal order of white-etching transformation and bearing cracks
open: Establish when white-etching microstructural transformation precedes bearing-crack initiation and when deformation around an existing crack produces it. Track the same inclusion and surrounding material through interrupted rolling-contact histories while controlling hydrogen, current, and sliding.
status: Dai and Long’s 2025 examination of failed wind-turbine bearings proposed a six-stage inclusion-associated failure sequence. Its chronology is inferred from postmortem structures; earlier rolling/sliding experiments support additional transformation pathways that require causal discrimination.
why: Prevention depends on whether white-etching transformation is a precursor, accelerator, or post-initiation signature.
key_works: R. Dai and H. Long (2025), “Formation mechanism of subsurface white etching area and white etching crack of failed bearings in wind turbine gearbox,” [DOI:10.1016/j.wear.2025.206335](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wear.2025.206335); H. Harada et al. (2005), “Microstructural Changes and Crack Initiation with White Etching Area Formation under Rolling/Sliding Contact in Bearing Steel,” [DOI:10.2355/isijinternational.45.1897](https://doi.org/10.2355/isijinternational.45.1897).

title: Interdiffusion-driven cavitation inside liquid solder pockets
open: Determine whether interdiffusion-induced tension nucleates cavities inside liquid solder before the liquid is consumed. Distinguish this mechanism from expansion of oxide films or entrained defects and from vacancy-driven voiding in solid intermetallics.
status: Kuziora and Aasmundtveit’s 2025 model predicts a cavitation criterion near −29 MPa for one 5 μm³ Ni–Sn solder pocket, reached after approximately six seconds under specified growth conditions. These are model outputs; actual liquid pressure and the operative void-initiation mechanism remain unmeasured.
why: It would show whether void suppression should target diffusion kinetics, liquid connectivity, or oxide cleanliness.
key_works: S. L. Kuziora and K. E. Aasmundtveit (2025; online 2024), “Solid–Liquid Diffusion Stresses Leading to Voiding,” [DOI:10.1007/s11661-024-07618-y](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11661-024-07618-y).

title: Birth and survival of sliver-forming dendrite fragments
open: Observe when a deformed dendrite detaches, rotates, survives remelting, and regrows as a sliver defect in a nickel-base single-crystal casting. Derive a fragment-survival criterion that distinguishes harmless bending from persistent competing-grain formation.
status: Yang and colleagues’ 2026 thermomechanical study connects slivers with localized plastic strain from inclined trunks and geometric protrusions. Fragmentation is implicated, but the complete detachment–transport–regrowth sequence and its survival threshold remain experimental targets.
why: It would enable blade geometries and solidification schedules that prevent slivers before final inspection.
key_works: L. Yang et al. (2026), “Dendrite deformation and fragmentation-induced sliver defects during solidification of nickel-based single-crystal superalloys,” [DOI:10.1016/j.scriptamat.2026.117399](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scriptamat.2026.117399).

title: Chunky graphite after high-superheat remelting
open: Explain why remelting low-sulfur ductile iron can produce chunky graphite even during subsequent chill casting. Determine whether its nuclei survive the melt or form anew, separating nucleant memory, magnesium fading, inoculant fading, and carbon supersaturation.
status: Adhiwiguna, Plück, and Deike’s 2025 study found strong thermal-history dependence over 1300–1500 °C remelting conditions. Magnesium and inoculant fading alone could not explain the resulting graphite sequence; disappearance of visible graphite does not establish removal of all heterogeneous precursors.
why: It would make recycled ductile-iron melt treatment more predictable.
key_works: I. B. G. S. Adhiwiguna, L. Plück, and R. Deike (2025; online 2024), “Vermicular and Chunky Graphite Nucleation during Chill Casting: Study on the Dynamics of Ductile Iron Recycling,” [DOI:10.1007/s40962-024-01473-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40962-024-01473-8).

title: Quantitative hydride contribution to anomalous magnesium hydrogen evolution
open: Determine whether transient MgH₂ accounts quantitatively for increased hydrogen evolution during anodic magnesium dissolution. Measure hydride formation and turnover alongside gas flux and metal loss, separating it from cathodic activation and alternative dissolution intermediates.
status: Gulbrandsen, Tucho, and Hansen’s 2026 experiments support a hydride-related interpretation and constrain charge accounting. The identity and causal role of reducing corrosion products remain hypotheses; gas produced during chemical analysis can also have non-hydride origins.
why: It would resolve which chemical pathways must be controlled to suppress magnesium corrosion and hydrogen production.
key_works: E. Gulbrandsen, W. M. Tucho, and V. Hansen (2026), “Searching for Evidence of Hydride Formation on Corroding Magnesium,” [DOI:10.5006/4919](https://doi.org/10.5006/4919).

title: Strengthening nickel–copper without reactivating metal dusting
open: Develop an alloying or dispersion-strengthening route that preserves copper’s suppression of carbon attack in Ni–Cu. Prevent strengthening additions from generating oxide–copper interfaces that catalyze CO dissociation and carbon ingress.
status: White and colleagues’ 2026 study found that manganese additions and TiN-containing variants could undermine protection associated with roughly 30 wt% copper. MnO–Cu and TiOₓ–Cu combinations promoted attack under carbon-rich conditions around 550–620 °C and 18–19 bar—a concrete negative result for otherwise attractive strengthening routes.
why: It would enable stronger components for synthesis-gas service without sacrificing corrosion resistance.
key_works: E. White, T. König, C. Schlereth, B. Öztürk, and M. Galetz (2026; online 2025), “How Mn and Ti Promote Metal Dusting in NiCu Alloys,” [DOI:10.1002/maco.70049](https://doi.org/10.1002/maco.70049).

title: Carbon ingress versus chromium depletion at supercritical-CO₂ breakaway
open: Determine whether breakaway oxidation in supercritical CO₂ begins through carbon-assisted chromium consumption, outward chromium loss, scale damage, or a coupled threshold. Resolve the order of carbide formation, protective-reservoir depletion, and local scale failure.
status: Ilinich and colleagues’ 2026 exposures extended to approximately 4,800 hours at 700 °C and 200 bar. HR120 underwent breakaway between roughly 1,500 and 2,000 hours; alloy-dependent spallation and subsurface changes complicate interpretation from mass gain alone. These are exposure-specific results, leaving the causal threshold unresolved.
why: A flux-based failure criterion would improve alloy selection for high-temperature CO₂ power cycles.
key_works: M. Ilinich et al. (2026), “The Effects of Extended Exposure to Supercritical CO2 on Select High-Performance Alloys,” [DOI:10.1021/acsomega.5c11290](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsomega.5c11290).

title: Lifetimes and dielectric weight of meron networks in PMN-based relaxors
open: Measure creation, annihilation, and persistence times of meron-like polarization textures in PMN and PMN–PT, and assign their contribution to frequency-dependent dielectric susceptibility. Distinguish a causal relaxation mechanism from topology reconstructed through equal-time correlations.
status: Eremenko and colleagues reconstructed three-dimensional polarization textures in 2025 using multiple scattering and local-structure measurements. The work concerns the cubic ergodic state; tracking individual textures in time and through low-temperature twinned phases remains unresolved.
why: It would establish whether useful relaxor response can be designed through topological-texture kinetics.
key_works: M. Eremenko et al. (2025), “Emergent topological polarization textures in relaxor ferroelectrics,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-62658-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62658-1).

title: Experimental disorder-free relaxor response from correlated polar skyrmions
open: Test whether interlayer correlations between polar skyrmions produce a broad, frequency-shifting dielectric maximum in a superlattice without quenched chemical disorder. Measure correlations and dielectric response together while excluding defect relaxation and an unrecognized structural transition.
status: Wang, Yang, and Chen proposed this mechanism through phase-field simulations in 2026, with a September revision. Their susceptibility maximum arises from competing correlation growth and polarization stiffness within the ferroelectric phase; experimental realization remains open.
why: It would offer a route to relaxor-like response through designed interactions and layer geometry.
key_works: Z. Wang, F. Yang, and L.-Q. Chen (2026), “Hidden Crossover and Relaxor-Like Response from Emerging Polar Skyrmion Correlations in Ferroelectric Superlattices,” [arXiv:2604.26100](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26100).

title: Three-dimensional selection rule for 71° wall annihilation during AC poling
open: Predict which 71° domain walls annihilate during alternating-current poling of rhombohedral relaxor–PT crystals, accounting for spacing, clamping, waveform, and three-dimensional junction geometry. Explain when 109° walls survive under the same protocol.
status: Sun and colleagues’ 2026 model finds selective annihilation and a geometry-dependent threshold in a simplified configuration. Real-time optical poling measurements also exist, but thickness-integrated imaging does not resolve the complete three-dimensional wall network needed to validate a transferable selection rule.
why: Poling protocols could be selected from starting microstructure instead of empirical training.
key_works: Y.-J. Sun et al. (2026), “Mesoscale Domain Evolution Mechanism during Alternating Current (AC) Poling of Relaxor Ferroelectrics,” [DOI:10.1002/adfm.76590](https://doi.org/10.1002/adfm.76590); Z. Wang et al. (2026), “Real-Time Ferroelectric Domain Wall Dynamics During Electric Poling and Depoling,” [DOI:10.1002/advs.76513](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.76513).

title: Stress-free zero-temperature ground state of PbZrO₃
open: Determine whether ideal, unstrained bulk PbZrO₃ has the conventional Pbam antiferroelectric ground state or a lower-energy ferrielectric arrangement. Resolve nuclear zero-point effects and kinetic trapping with agreement beyond a single density functional.
status: The question sharpened in 2021 when calculations placed competing structures within small energy differences. Ferrielectric–antiferroelectric coexistence was stabilized experimentally through strain in 2024, but strained-film accessibility does not identify the equilibrium zero-stress bulk ground state.
why: The reference antiferroelectric’s actual ground state affects interpretations of switching and energy-storage pathways.
key_works: H. Aramberri et al. (2021), “On the possibility that PbZrO3 not be antiferroelectric,” [DOI:10.1038/s41524-021-00671-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41524-021-00671-w); Z. Yu et al. (2024), “Room-temperature stabilizing strongly competing ferrielectric and antiferroelectric phases in PbZrO3 by strain-mediated phase separation,” [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47776-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-47776-6).

title: Closing the PST–PMW electrocaloric regenerator efficiency gap
open: Demonstrate sustained refrigeration below room temperature using PST–PMW multilayer capacitors while measuring complete electrical and thermal energy balances. Include recovered electrical work, inactive mass, heat-transfer losses, and pumping.
status: Guo and colleagues reported approximately 3 K electrocaloric changes in 2026 and more than 10⁷ field applications at 17.1 V μm⁻¹ without breakdown. PMW substitution also removed a lengthy ordering anneal; the reported high regenerator efficiencies are ideal-cycle calculations with work recovery, leaving whole-device performance to establish.
why: It would determine whether the improved ceramic produces efficient practical refrigeration.
key_works: M. Guo et al. (2026), “Electrocaloric effects across room temperature in multilayer capacitors,” [DOI:10.1038/s41586-026-10492-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10492-w).

title: Low-stress elastocaloric cooling with texture-enabled endurance
open: Retain roughly 15 K adiabatic cooling and 10⁷-cycle endurance in precipitate-engineered TiNi while reducing approximately 900 MPa actuation stress by an order of magnitude. This combined specification is a proposed census milestone, to be met in the same specimen and protocol.
status: Li and colleagues demonstrated −15.9 K after ten million compressive cycles in 2026 using textured TiNi containing Ti₄Ni₂O precipitates. Those measurements involved unloading from 900 MPa; the proposed combination with much lower stress remains unmet by that result.
why: Lower force would reduce actuator and structural hardware while preserving cooling density.
